subject: Renewal Offer: Dedicated Capacity Increase and Isolation Plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>, Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal + dedicated pool expansion — initial terms

Samantha / Luis —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, we built a renewal proposal that includes the dedicated GPU reservation increase you requested and a tenant-isolation plan for the expanded pool. High level summary:

- Term: 12 months (renewal start 2027-11-01)
- Additional reserved capacity: +8 A100-80GB equivalents (configurable as 8x8g or 4x16g pods)
- Isolation: logically fenced reserved pool with per-tenant QoS and KV-cache partitioning; optionally colocated on separate AZs
- Throughput target (contracted): baseline 11,000 tokens/sec aggregate with autoscale burst to 22,000 tokens/sec for 10 minutes; p95 inference latency target <220ms for 512-token requests
- Price: outlined in attached proposal_pricing_sheet.xlsx and SOW (attached)

Next steps I recommend: 1) review the attached SOW and isolation_runbook_v2; 2) confirm if AtlasHealth needs an on-prem private deployment for the isolated pool or if dedicated hosted with logical fencing is sufficient; 3) procurement to confirm PO cadence so we can lock the launch window in November.

I attached the SOW, the runbook (isolation runbook v2) and a network diagram for the proposed tenant fencing. Rishi is copied to scope the technical onboarding; he can run a short technical walkthrough with your infra team.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: SOW_AtlasHealth_2027Q4.pdf (proposal and T&Cs), isolation_runbook_v2.docx (ops runbook), network_diagram.png

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + dedicated pool expansion — initial terms

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and attachments. A few clarifying items from our side before procurement takes it to legal: 

1) Isolation: we want a guarantee that our model weights and KV cache won't be accessible to other tenants and that noisy neighbors can't affect our latency below the contracted p95. Can you confirm what "logical fencing" entails operationally and how you validate it?

2) Throughput: the numbers look promising. We need a short definition of the baseline vs burst behavior (how often burst is permitted and what triggers it). Also want a p99 latency target called out for SLAs if possible.

3) Migration window: if we sign in October, what's the earliest the expanded pool will be live? We need it before a product launch in mid-December.

Happy for Rishi to run the tech walkthrough — Luis will join the call for the architecture discussion.

Samantha Lee
VP Product, AtlasHealth
Samantha.Lee@atlashealth.com

[Procurement note: procurement@atlashealth.com — please advise on required PO wording and if Atlas needs a separate order for reserved pool expansion.]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + dedicated pool expansion — initial terms

Samantha / Luis —

Appreciate the questions — quick answers, and I've attached a short ops checklist in the runbook for validation steps we run with customers: 

Isolation (logical fencing) — what it means operationally:
- Dedicated reserved pool (isolated scheduling domain) with tenant-tagged placement so Atlas workloads never share GPUs with non-Atlas tenants.
- KV-cache partitioning and namespace enforcement: KV keys scoped to tenant namespace; eviction/garbage-collection policies per namespace.
- Network isolation via private VPC peering; optional strict egress rules and customer-managed IP allowlist.
- Audit logs and instance-level access controls; we can provide instance metadata and process lists for verification during onboarding.

Validation and proof points we provide:
- Pre-launch smoke tests showing tenant-only placement (we record hostnames and instance ids)
- A short load test run (we run a 90-minute synthetic load to validate throughput and p95/p99 targets)
- Post-launch 72-hour monitoring summary with token/sec and latency percentiles

Throughput baseline vs burst:
- Baseline is the guaranteed sustained aggregate capacity for the reserved pool (11k tokens/sec).
- Burst is a short-duration autoscale up to 22k tokens/sec; burst budget measured in token-seconds per billing period (we recommend monthly token-second budget and call out expected frequency).
- We can include a p99 latency objective in the contract as a target (we typically do p95 SLAs with credits; p99 SLAs require larger committed capacity or different pricing—I included options in the SOW appendix).

Migration window:
- If contracts are signed by 2027-10-10 and PO is received, target provisioning = 21 business days (so live by end of November). We can prioritize your launch for an extra ramp fee or by shifting capacity from upcoming maintenance windows.

Next step: Marissa, procurement, can we aim for PO + signed SOW by Oct 7 to hit the timeline? I can schedule the technical walkthrough week of Sep 20.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + dedicated pool expansion — initial terms

Team —

This looks workable. A couple of procurement/legal asks we know up front:
- We need the runbook excerpt that explains host-level separation and the sample audit report format (for our security team).
- Please confirm the failure mode: if we exceed burst budget, will requests be throttled or failover to a lower-cost model? We need deterministic behavior rather than opaque throttling.

Assuming those are addressed in the SOW, procurement will prepare a PO. We will also want a short clause about incident response time for severity-1 service degradations during the first 90 days after migration.

Luis Ramirez
CTO, AtlasHealth
Luis.Ramirez@atlashealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@atlashealth.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal offer: Dedicated Capacity Increase and Isolation Plan

Luis / Samantha / procurement —

Thanks — quick confirmations inline and next steps: 

- Runbook excerpt + sample audit report: attached (isolation_runbook_v2.docx includes the host-level separation section and a sample audit report template).
- Failure mode when burst budget is exhausted: requests are routed to the contracted base capacity and excess requests are queued for up to 30s. We also support a configurable fallback policy to route overflow traffic to a cost-tier model variant (documented in the SOW appendix). We'll add explicit language to the SOW stating queuing behavior and the optional model-fallback path.
- Incident response clause: we will include a 90-day elevated incident SLA in the SOW appendix with a 1-hour response for sev-1 callbacks and a named escalation path (Rishi and a dedicated on-call engineering contact).

Procurement — if you can confirm required PO wording by Oct 1, Marissa will get the final SOW and a DocuSign envelope over the week of Oct 3. We can also schedule the technical walkthrough Sep 22 at 10:00 PT (Rishi will run through validation steps and a sample load test plan).

I'll follow up with the DocuSign link and a short checklist for the onboarding call.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Marissa.Cole@redwood.com
